title: Districts and related organizations run by the same people
question: Where a district and another organization share board members or managers, is the tie on the record, and how much City money goes to each?
finding: 3 pairs share people and have a second link on file. SF Tourism Improvement Dist Mgmt Corp and San Francisco Travel Association: 14 people on both returns, 3 of them on the payroll of one (EVP, COO; EVP, Chief Financial Officer); apart from assessments the City paid the first $39.4 million and the second $13.0 million, and the returns record $45.9 million passing between them. Union Square Foundation and Union Square Business Improvmnt District: 13 people on both returns, 8 of them on the payroll of one (Assoc, Finance/HR; Assoc, Marketing; CEO; Deputy Director); apart from assessments the City paid the first $5.6 million and the second $2.9 million, and the returns record $5.7 million passing between them. No of Market/Tenderloin Com Benefit Corp and Mid Market Foundation: 3 people on both returns, 1 of them on the payroll of one (Executive Dir.); apart from assessments the City paid the first $16.3 million and the second $82.4 million, and the returns record $2.2 million passing between them. 19 further pairs share at least one name on their boards with no other link on file; they are not listed, because a shared name alone is not evidence of the same person.
how: Officers, directors and key employees listed on the returns (Part VII) of each district organization, of every organization a district declares as related (Schedule R), and of every organization that names a district as a paid contractor. Two returns “share” a person when the same first and last name appears on both: a name match. A pair is listed only when the returns themselves supply a second link: one declares the other as a related organization, or one reports paying the other. Money between them is what those schedules report; where both sides report the same year, the larger side’s total is used. No individual is named in this screen; roles are given for people one of the two organizations pays.
limits: A district with a separate foundation staffed by the district’s own employees is using an ordinary structure, and the tax form exists to disclose exactly this. People who own or manage property downtown can sit on several of these boards for that reason alone. The question is only whether City grants to one organization and assessments to its twin pay for the same staff twice, which the returns do not show. What would settle it: the cost-sharing agreement between the two and the grant budgets.
